issues.legal_issue: The term “house” in the village tax provision includes factory buildings and is not limited to dwelling houses.
material_facts: The village panchayat imposed a tax on houses and lands under a 1952 resolution, before the statute replaced “houses” with “buildings” in 1954.
The tax demands at issue concerned factory buildings.

Rules made under the statute used “lands and buildings” where the statute referred to “lands and houses,” and later rules defined a house as any building or set of buildings within the same enclosure.
The statutory scheme treated the tax on houses and lands separately from optional taxes on businesses such as shops and hotels and on premises where machinery was used for trade or business.
issues.conclusion: The term “houses” in the statutory tax provision includes all buildings, including factory buildings, irrespective of their use.
issues.legal_principle: An undefined statutory word is construed in the sense that people conversant with the subject matter would attribute to it, having regard to the context and purpose of the statute (Ramavtar v. Assistant Sales Tax Officer; Motipur Zamindari Co. v. State of Bihar). In taxing and municipal legislation, “house” can include a business building and is not confined to a dwelling house; the Court relied on Yorkshire Insurance v. Clayton, Grant v. Langston, Daniel v. Coulsting, Folkestone v. Woodward, Wimbledon Urban District Council v. Hastings, Ravenseft Properties v. London Borough of Hillingdon, and Corpus Juris Secundum. Rules made under the statute and placed before the legislature are a legitimate aid as contemporanea expositio. The later substitution of “buildings” made explicit what was implicit in the earlier wording. A statement of objects and reasons is ordinarily not an aid to construction, though it may be consulted in the limited circumstances described by the Court.

predicates.village_tax_case: The proceeding concerns a village authority’s tax imposed under a statutory scheme for village taxation.
predicates.undefined_house_term: The governing tax provision uses the term “house” without defining it.
predicates.contemporaneous_rules_treat_houses_as_bu: Rules made under the governing scheme use “buildings” in the corresponding tax context or define a house to include a building.
predicates.statutory_scheme_taxes_houses_and_lands_: The statutory scheme distinguishes the tax on houses and lands from separate taxes on business activity or business premises.

issues.definition: When a village tax case involves an undefined term “house,” contemporaneous rules equate that term with buildings, and the statutory scheme separately taxes houses and lands from business activity, the term covers all buildings.

issues.legal_issue: A valid earlier tax resolution continues to support tax demands when a later resolution did not supersede or modify it and the tax is consistent with the successor statute.
material_facts: The panchayat validly passed a 1952 resolution imposing the tax under the then-governing statute.
A 1964 resolution revised the tax rate, but the Court found that no levy on the factory buildings was imposed pursuant to that resolution and that it did not supersede or modify the 1952 resolution.
The demands were made under the 1952 resolution.
The 1959 successor statute preserved existing taxes that were not inconsistent with it, and the Court found no inconsistency.
issues.conclusion: The tax demands were valid under the 1952 resolution, notwithstanding the asserted invalidity of the 1964 resolution.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 186(8) of the Bombay Village Panchayats Act, 1958 (Act III of 1959), an existing tax that is not inconsistent with the successor Act is deemed to have been imposed under that Act and continues until superseded or modified. The earlier resolution remained operative because the later resolution neither superseded nor modified it, and the demands were made under the earlier resolution.

rule.if: tax_demand_appeal and earlier_tax_resolution_valid and demands_made_under_earlier_resolution and later_resolution_did_not_supersede_earlier_resolution and earlier_tax_consistent_with_successor_law

predicates.tax_demand_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging demands for a tax imposed by a public authority.
predicates.earlier_tax_resolution_valid: The public authority validly adopted an earlier resolution imposing the tax.
predicates.demands_made_under_earlier_resolution: The challenged demands were made pursuant to the earlier resolution.
predicates.later_resolution_did_not_supersede_earli: A later resolution did not supersede or modify the earlier resolution or impose the challenged tax in its place.
predicates.earlier_tax_consistent_with_successor_la: The tax imposed under the earlier resolution is not inconsistent with the successor law.

issues.definition: If an appeal challenges tax demands made under a valid earlier resolution, a later resolution did not replace it, and the tax is consistent with the successor law, the demands remain valid.
